- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >79), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (e.g., -0.28 or -0.22) in last 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 2–3% to forecast to counteract bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in 10–15 day horizon; apply 1.5–2.5% upward bias for medium-term forecasts.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.06–0.17) and price is trending upward, model lags; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period spikes (last 5–7 days); adjust final 5–7 entries upward by 1–3% if sentiment is positive or volatile.
